## Purpose

This SOP describes the determination of soil microbial biomass carbon (MBC) using the chloroform fumigation-extraction (CFE) method. Chloroform vapor lyses microbial cells, releasing intracellular carbon that is then extracted with 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ and quantified as dissolved organic carbon (DOC).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Field-moist soil samples collected per SOP-F02 for microbial biomass assessment
- **Does not apply to:** Air-dried or frozen soils (unless pre-validated for this method); microbial biomass nitrogen (requires additional analytical steps)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve protocol, ensure safety compliance              |
| Trained Personnel | Perform fumigation and extraction, report results       |
| New Students      | Complete training and safety orientation before use     |

## Definitions

- **Chloroform fumigation-extraction (CFE):** The standard method for measuring soil microbial biomass carbon; soil is fumigated with ethanol-free chloroform to lyse microbial cells, then extracted with K~2~SO~4~; microbial biomass C is calculated as the difference in extractable C between fumigated and unfumigated soils divided by an efficiency factor ($k_{EC}$).
- **Extractable organic carbon (EOC):** The organic carbon recovered from soil in K~2~SO~4~ extract; includes a background pool of soluble organic carbon from non-microbial sources as well as carbon released from lysed microbial cells.
- **$k_{EC}$ factor:** The extraction efficiency correction factor for microbial biomass carbon; commonly 0.45 (meaning 45% of lysed microbial carbon is recovered in the extract); must be specified when reporting results [@vance1987].
- **Microbial biomass carbon (MBC):** The total carbon contained in the living soil microbial community (bacteria, fungi, protozoa, nematodes); expressed as mg C kg^-1^ dry soil; a key indicator of soil biological health and nutrient cycling potential.
- **Potentially mineralizable nitrogen (PMN):** The nitrogen that can be released from soil organic matter by microbial activity under aerobic conditions; correlated with microbial biomass and organic matter quality.
- **Unfumigated control:** Soil extracted with K~2~SO~4~ without prior chloroform fumigation; provides the background extractable carbon value that is subtracted from the fumigated extract to calculate microbial biomass C.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-danger}
### Critical Safety Warning

Chloroform (CHCl~3~) is a volatile, toxic solvent and a suspected carcinogen. All fumigation steps must be performed inside a fume hood. Do not inhale chloroform vapors. Use ethanol-free chloroform only.
:::

### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Chloroform (toxic, volatile); 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ (mild irritant)
- **Physical:** Vacuum desiccator under reduced pressure; glassware breakage

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (double-glove recommended when handling chloroform)
- [ ] Safety glasses or goggles
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Work in fume hood at all times during fumigation

### Emergency Procedures

In case of chloroform spill, refer to the SDS and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd). Evacuate the area if spill is large; ventilate the space and notify the supervisor.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Notes                                        |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|
| Vacuum desiccator             | Glass, with stopcock and vacuum line         |
| Vacuum pump                   | Oil-free preferred                           |
| Fume hood                     | Required for all chloroform handling         |
| Orbital or end-over-end shaker | For extraction step                         |
| Centrifuge                    | Capable of 4000 x g (optional)              |
| Filtration apparatus          | With 0.45 um glass fiber filters             |
| Analytical balance            | 0.01 g resolution                           |
| Incubator or dark cabinet     | For 24-hour fumigation at room temperature  |
| TOC analyzer                  | Shimadzu TOC-L or equivalent (see SOP-L06)  |

### Reagents and Consumables

| Item                          | Notes                                        |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|
| Ethanol-free chloroform       | ACS grade; stored in fume hood              |
| 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ solution     | Prepare fresh or within 1 week              |
| Glass fiber filters (0.45 um) | Pre-combusted at 450 C for 4 hours          |
| Boiling chips or glass beads  | For chloroform evaporation under vacuum     |
| Extraction bottles (100 mL)   | Screw-top, HDPE or glass                    |
| Filter funnels and flasks     | Clean, acid-washed                          |
| Sample vials                  | For filtered extracts, acid-washed          |


## Procedure

### Preparation

1. Prepare 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ by dissolving 87.1 g K~2~SO~4~ per liter of deionized water
2. Pre-combust glass fiber filters at 450 C for 4 hours and store in a clean container
3. Determine the gravimetric moisture content of a separate subsample (dry at 105 C for 24 hours) so results can be expressed on a dry-weight basis

### Fumigation

1. Weigh two paired subsamples of 15 g field-moist soil into labeled extraction bottles
2. Place one set (fumigated) into the vacuum desiccator inside the fume hood
3. Place a beaker containing approximately 30 mL of ethanol-free chloroform and a few boiling chips in the center of the desiccator
4. Evacuate the desiccator using the vacuum pump until the chloroform begins to boil vigorously (approximately 2 minutes)
5. Close the stopcock and incubate in the dark at room temperature (approximately 25 C) for 24 hours
6. The second set (unfumigated controls) is extracted immediately (proceed to 6.3)

### Extraction

1. After 24 hours, release the vacuum in the fume hood and remove the chloroform beaker
2. Evacuate the desiccator repeatedly (3--5 times) to remove residual chloroform vapor from the soil
3. Add 60 mL of 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ to each bottle (both fumigated and unfumigated), achieving a 1:4 soil-to-extractant ratio
4. Cap bottles and shake on an orbital or end-over-end shaker for 1 hour
5. Allow the suspension to settle briefly, or centrifuge at 4000 x g for 10 minutes
6. Filter the supernatant through a pre-combusted 0.45 um glass fiber filter into a clean sample vial
7. Store filtered extracts at 4 C if not analyzed immediately (analyze within 48 hours)

### DOC Analysis

1. Analyze filtered extracts for dissolved organic carbon using the Shimadzu TOC-L (see SOP-L06) or equivalent TOC analyzer
2. Run 0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ blanks alongside samples

### Calculation

Microbial biomass carbon is calculated as:

$$
\text{MBC} = \frac{C_{\text{fumigated}} - C_{\text{unfumigated}}}{k_C}
$$

where:

- $C_{\text{fumigated}}$ = DOC in the fumigated extract (mg C kg^-1^ dry soil)
- $C_{\text{unfumigated}}$ = DOC in the unfumigated extract (mg C kg^-1^ dry soil)
- $k_C$ = 0.45, the extraction efficiency coefficient (Vance et al., 1987)

::: {.callout-note}
The unfumigated extract DOC value represents the background dissolved organic carbon pool and is often reported separately as an indicator of labile soil carbon.
:::


## Quality Control

- Run analytical triplicates for at least 10% of samples
- Include a reagent blank (0.5 M K~2~SO~4~ only, no soil) in each batch
- Include a laboratory reference soil in each batch to monitor method consistency
- Verify that the coefficient of variation among replicates is less than 15%

| Waste Type                   | Container              | Disposal Method               |
|:-----------------------------|:-----------------------|:------------------------------|
| Chloroform waste             | Halogenated waste jug  | EH&S hazardous waste pickup   |
| K~2~SO~4~ extracts           | Aqueous waste container | Drain with copious water (if approved) or collect for EH&S |
| Used soil                    | Solid waste bag        | Standard trash                |
| Used glass fiber filters     | Standard trash         | Standard trash                |

## Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd) in full
2. Review the SDS for chloroform
3. Observe a trained operator perform the full fumigation-extraction procedure
4. Demonstrate competence with vacuum desiccator operation
5. Perform the procedure under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
